§10.1 Forms and Key-Value Regions

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-forms-and-key-value-regions · forms

✅ Normative

Fill-in fields and checkbox regions are key-value content, not tables: they MUST be rendered as the key-value list of The Key-Value List§10.3.2 and MUST NOT be rendered as a table. The output MUST NOT contain a two-column key/value table that the page does not print as a ruled grid.

Form controls printed on the page — labels waiting for a value, checkbox rows, signature and date lines — look tabular because they line up in columns. They are not tables: the alignment is typesetting, not structure.

Insurer: ________        NAIC #: ________
☒ Renewal     ☐ New business

- **Insurer:** [blank]
- **NAIC #:** [blank]
- [x] Renewal
- [ ] New business

Fillable or static

A region is form content when it prints labelled fields to fill, checkboxes, or blanks — even when its layout looks like a plain grid of labels and values. Such a region MUST be rendered as a key-value list.

A static key-value reference — a legend, a specification sheet, a summary box, filing metadata — prints fixed labels and values and nothing to fill in and no checkbox. It is not a form. The test is whether anything on it was meant to be filled in.

The border test for static key-value blocks

A page that raises this question is usually half form, half grid, so the decision is made region by region. For each static block of label: value pairs:

The block Rendering
Printed inside a ruled border (a gridded key/value block) It MUST be rendered as a table, per Is This Even a Table§9.1.5; leaving it out drops a table.
Not ruled — a specification stack, a cluster of Label: value fields above a table, an address block, a prose-line legend It MUST be rendered as text in reading order and MUST NOT be rendered as a table.

A totals block printed under a table is the one exception: it belongs to the table above it, not to the surrounding fields — see Bottom Edge Totals and Islands§9.7.1.

✅ Sample — ratefiling

SERFF filing metadata as ungridded Label: value fields above two genuine ruled tables on the same page. Nothing on the page is fillable, so the fields are static text lines; only the two ruled grids are tables.

Why not a small table

A two-column key/value table built from an unruled block creates a record that exists nowhere on the page — the never invent failure of Never Drop, Never Invent§2.2. It teaches whatever learns from the output that structure can be conjured from whitespace. Rendering the block as text or as a key-value list loses nothing, because nothing there was ever printed as tabular.

Related

  • The Key-Value List§10.3.2 — how form content is transcribed once it is recognised
  • Is This Even a Table§9.1.5 — the test a ruled static block goes through
  • Marks and Symbols in Cells§9.6.6 — checkbox glyphs used as values inside a real table cell
  • Empty Pre-Printed Grids§9.1.3 — a fully blank ruled form, where the structure is the content
